title: Parts of a Plant Cell
description: Middle school science: the organelles of a plant cell, then a close-up of a chloroplast.

steps.label: Cell wall
steps.text: The **cell wall** is a stiff layer of cellulose around the outside. It supports the cell and gives it a boxy shape.

steps.label: Cell membrane
steps.text: The thin **cell membrane** lines the inside of the wall. It controls what enters and leaves the cell.

steps.label: Cytoplasm
steps.text: **Cytoplasm** is the jelly-like fluid that fills the cell. The organelles sit in it.

steps.label: Nucleus
steps.text: The **nucleus** holds the cell's DNA. It directs the cell's growth and activities.

steps.label: Central vacuole
steps.text: The large **central vacuole** stores water. When it is full, it presses on the wall and keeps the plant firm.

steps.label: Chloroplast
steps.text: **Chloroplasts** make food from sunlight. Animal cells do not have them.

steps.label: Mitochondrion
steps.text: **Mitochondria** break down sugar to release energy the cell can use.

question.text: Which organelle is found in plant cells but not in animal cells?

steps.label: Double membrane
steps.text: Two membranes wrap the chloroplast. Together they form the **envelope**, which controls what moves in and out.

steps.label: Granum
steps.text: A **granum** is a stack of thylakoids, like a stack of coins. One chloroplast holds many grana.

steps.label: Thylakoid
steps.text: Each flat disc is a **thylakoid**. Its membrane holds chlorophyll, the green pigment that absorbs light.

steps.label: Stroma
steps.text: The **stroma** is the fluid around the grana. Here the chloroplast builds sugar from carbon dioxide and water.

question.text: Put these in order from largest to smallest.
Match each part to its job.

welcomeMessage: Name the parts of a plant cell and what each part does.
